answer.summary: No prior evidence in Kumar et al., 2024 supports memory mechanisms beyond detectable state triggers under perturbations or low-variation input sequences.
answer.content: Current analysis shows absence of explicit memory mechanisms in Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1 across retrieval, encoding, and coherence domains. A new, narrow inquiry must focus on a distinct dimension: the persistence of memory state under gradual, non-disruptive input drift without predefined feature vectors or external cues. This tests whether any form of implicit continuity can be observed in sequence behavior under slow change, independent of abrupt perturbations or noise events.
